info.name: Shree Astro — Astrologer App
info.description:
Everything **astro_app** calls.

## Start here
1. Select the **Shree Astro — Local** environment.
2. Run *2 · Application* top to bottom: register → upload a document → add a bank account → submit. You must attach a real file on the two upload requests (tick the `file` row).
3. Approve the application with the **Admin Panel** collection — the `astrologerId` is already saved for it.
4. Come back and go online, then take a consultation.

## Two things that will confuse you otherwise
**You cannot take work until an admin approves you.** Before that you are not in the seeker's directory at all, so a request can never arrive.

**You cannot set your own rate.** Rates are requested here and written only when an admin approves the request.

## Auth
Requests inherit `Authorization: Bearer {{astroAccessToken}}`. Sign-in saves it for you. A 401 with `code: "token_expired"` means refresh and retry.

item.name: 2 · Application

request.description:
Personal Info + Professional Details, sent as one request. This creates the account and signs the astrologer in — the rest of the wizard is filed against it with a token.

The account starts at `professional_submitted` and **cannot take consultations until an admin approves it**. It is not in the seeker's directory yet either.

`languages` and `expertise` are ids from models/constants.js. Send them as repeated form rows (Postman does this automatically for the two rows below).

Refusals: 409 if the number already has an application.

formdata.description: 10 digits — this is the login number
Repeat this row for each language
Repeat this row for each area

formdata.value: Vedic astrologer with 18 years of practice.

item.name: 3 · Signing in

request.description:
Sends a 6-digit code.

No SMS/email provider is wired up yet, so outside production the real code comes back as `devCode` and is also printed to the server log. This request saves it to `{{devCode}}`, so the next request works without copying anything.

`role` says which app is asking. `channel` is `phone` or `email`.

Refusals: 404 `account_not_found` (not registered — send them to Register), 403 `account_blocked`, 429 `otp_cooldown` (a code was sent less than 30s ago; `retryAfterSeconds` says how long to wait).

exec: const save = (k, v) => (pm.environment.name ? pm.environment.set(k, v) : pm.collectionVariables.set(k, v));

request.description:
Trades the code for a session and saves both tokens.

`{{devCode}}` was filled in by the previous request. `{{masterOtp}}` (123456) also works for any account while there is no SMS provider — swap it in to skip step 1 entirely.

Refusals: 400 wrong code (the message says how many attempts are left), 400 expired, 429 `otp_attempts_exceeded` after 5 wrong guesses — a resend clears the lockout.

exec: const save = (k, v) => (pm.environment.name ? pm.environment.set(k, v) : pm.collectionVariables.set(k, v));

request.description:
Call this when a request answers 401 with `code: "token_expired"` — that means refresh and retry, not sign out. Any other 401 means the session is dead.

A browser sends the cookie automatically; the apps post the refresh token in the body.

request.description: Clears the cookies the admin panel uses. The apps hold no cookies, so signing out there is a local act: delete both tokens from the keystore. Tokens stay valid until they expire.

request.description:
The whole dashboard in one call — today's earnings, the performance card, the services card and how many requests are waiting.

`missing` lists any profile fields still to fill in, which is what an admin-created account uses to nudge for exactly the right things.
Everything the profile screen shows, plus `applicationStatus`, `onboardingStep` (which step to resume on) and, if rejected, `rejectionReason`.
Every field is optional. Multipart, so a new photo can ride along.

formdata.value: Vedic astrologer with 18 years of practice.

request.description:
The dashboard's availability toggle. Only an online astrologer can receive requests.

Holding a socket also marks you online automatically, and the last socket disconnecting marks you offline — closing one device does not sign you off another.

**Works once.** While the profile is still being set up there is no agreed price to change, so the astrologer sets their own opening rates here.

The moment the profile is complete — nothing left in `missing` — this is refused with 400, and every change after that goes through *Request a price change* for an admin to approve.

`GET /astrologer/me` tells you which state you are in via `canSetOwnRates`.
What the Price Change screen's table shows: the live rate for each service, and any request still being reviewed.

exec: const save = (k, v) => (pm.environment.name ? pm.environment.set(k, v) : pm.collectionVariables.set(k, v));

request.description:
Turns a service on or off, or changes the free minutes granted to a first-time seeker.

**The rate cannot be set here** — that is what the price-change request is for. `type` is `chat`, `call`, `live_chat`, `live_call` or `emergency_chat`.

Files a new rate for an admin to approve. The rate only actually changes when they approve it — this is the **only** way a rate ever changes.

`applyToAll` sets the same rate on every service. 409 if a request for that service is already being reviewed.

Raises it with an admin as unfair. It toggles, and un-flagging gives the allowance back.

Flags are rationed — the answer carries `flagsRemaining`, the monthly allowance the My Reviews screen prints — so this cannot be used to bury every bad review.

Minimum ₹100. The money leaves the withdrawable balance **immediately** and sits in `pendingWithdrawal` until an admin decides — so the same money cannot be requested twice.

Omit `bankAccountId` to use the primary account. The account must already be approved, and rejecting a request puts the money back.
